items.title: VS Code Shortcuts That Save Hours (Multi-Cursor, Move Lines, Command Palette for Beginners)
items.description:
The VS Code keyboard shortcuts that save hours, shown for Windows, Linux and Mac side by side: open any file in a second, move and copy whole lines, edit many places at once with multiple cursors, and rename safely with F2. Step by step for beginners, including the Ctrl+D mistake that silently changes the wrong words, and every result on screen is the real output of the code shown.

Chapters
0:00 The result
0:26 Why shortcuts matter
0:42 The plan
0:57 Ctrl vs Cmd
1:11 Ctrl+P: open any file
1:33 Ctrl+G and the terminal
1:53 Ctrl+Shift+P: the Command Palette
2:11 Move a line: Alt+Up/Down
2:24 Copy a line: Shift+Alt+Down
2:44 Comment and delete lines
3:28 Multiple cursors: Ctrl+D
3:49 The mistake: selecting by hand first
4:13 Ctrl+Shift+L: all matches at once
4:47 Cursor below: Ctrl+Alt+Down
5:38 Rename safely: F2
6:13 Other common mistakes
6:35 Cheat sheet
6:56 Pro tips
7:29 How to make them stick
7:48 Recap

Shortcuts (Windows / Linux  |  Mac)
Ctrl+P  |  Cmd+P  -  Quick Open: jump to any file
Ctrl+Shift+P (or F1)  |  Cmd+Shift+P  -  Command Palette: every command
Ctrl+G  |  Ctrl+G  -  Go to line
Ctrl+B  |  Cmd+B  -  Show / hide the sidebar
Ctrl+`  |  Ctrl+`  -  Open the terminal
Alt+Up / Alt+Down  |  Option+Up / Option+Down  -  Move the line
Shift+Alt+Down  |  Shift+Option+Down  -  Copy the line (Linux: Ctrl+Shift+Alt+Down)
Ctrl+/  |  Cmd+/  -  Comment / uncomment
Ctrl+Shift+K  |  Cmd+Shift+K  -  Delete the line
Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X with nothing selected  -  Copy / cut the whole line
Ctrl+D  |  Cmd+D  -  Select the word, then add the next match
Ctrl+Shift+L  |  Cmd+Shift+L  -  Select all matches
Ctrl+Alt+Down  |  Cmd+Option+Down  -  Add a cursor below (Linux: Shift+Alt+Down)
Alt+Click  |  Option+Click  -  Add a cursor anywhere
End  |  Cmd+Right  -  Jump to end of line (works with many cursors)
Ctrl+Enter / Ctrl+Shift+Enter  |  Cmd+Enter / Cmd+Shift+Enter  -  New line below / above
F2  -  Rename symbol (code only, not comments or text)
Shift+Alt+Right  |  Ctrl+Shift+Cmd+Right  -  Expand selection
Ctrl+K then Ctrl+S  |  Cmd+K then Cmd+S  -  Keyboard Shortcuts editor

The Ctrl+D mistake
Start Ctrl+D from a plain cursor inside the word: it matches the whole word with the same upper/lower case.
If you select the text by hand first, Ctrl+D follows the Find options (by default: any case, also inside other words), so "total" also grabs "Total" and "Subtotal".

cart.py (start)
prices = {
    "apple": 1.20,
    "bread": 2.50,
    "milk": 0.99,
}
tax = 0.08

total = sum(prices.values())
print("Total:", round(total * (1 + tax), 2))
print("Subtotal:", round(total, 2))
print("DEBUG", prices)

cart.py (after the shortcuts)
prices = {
    "apple": 1.20,
    "bread": 2.50,
    "milk": 0.99,
    "eggs": 3.10,
}
TAX = 0.08

subtotal = sum(prices.values())
print("Subtotal:", round(subtotal, 2))
print("Total:", round(subtotal * (1 + TAX), 2))

list.py (start: one word per line)
apple
bread
milk
eggs
coffee

list.py (after multiple cursors)
items = [
    "apple",
    "bread",
    "milk",
    "eggs",
    "coffee",
]
print(len(items), "items:", ", ".join(items))

report.py (after F2 rename)
# calc: quantity times price
def line_total(qty, price):
    return qty * price

orders = [("apple", 3, 1.20), ("milk", 2, 0.99)]
print("calc for each order:")
for name, qty, price in orders:
    print(name, line_total(qty, price))
